races.name: Hazelton Mountford Insurance Brokers Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Rebel Tribesman
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent form who should get ideal position tracking Bathara without making the running himself
runners_data.comment: Just touched off when a short-priced favourite in a couple of Sedgefield maidens.
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper at Aintree last May; changed hands subsequently and has just been touched off when a short-priced favourite in a couple of Sedgefield maidens over 2m1f since switching to hurdles; steps up in trip and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Mr Rafiki
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed improved staying power at Ffos Las after wind surgery and may benefit from stronger pace here
runners_data.comment: Stayed on well when fourth in a Ffos Las maiden last month on hurdles debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Last of four in a Ludlow bumper in October; had wind surgery subsequently and stayed on well when fourth of ten finishers in a Ffos Las maiden (2m4f, good to soft) last month on hurdles debut; that was a step in the right direction but more is required here.

runners_data.name: Bathara
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who gets uncontested lead but form over hurdles is disappointing despite bumper win at this course
runners_data.comment: Landed bumper here last October but has cut little ice in his two starts over hurdles.
runners_data.spotlight: Landed bumper around here last October but has cut little ice in his two starts over hurdles; this looks easier but he needs to start producing.

runners_data.name: Royal Rocket
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner going the right way after decent Taunton third but may lack the class edge in better company
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on his hurdles debut to finish third in a Taunton novice last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on his hurdles debut at Chepstow to finish third of seven in a Taunton novice (2m3f, good) last month; is going the right way and holds claims, but his best chance of success will be in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Blue's Secret Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who flopped on hurdles debut 16 days ago and may struggle for racing room given her running style
runners_data.comment: Finished last of seven on hurdles debut at Fakenham 16 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed ability when in the frame in a couple of bumpers but finished last of seven on hurdles debut at Fakenham (2m4f, good) 16 days ago; may not come into her own until she is qualified for handicaps.

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making hurdles debut with solid Flat credentials but untested over obstacles in competitive company
runners_data.comment: Made a pleasing hurdles debut when third in a Hereford maiden 15 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: A nine-time Flat winner over 1m6f-2m, he made a pleasing hurdles debut when third of five finishers (with stablemate Alex The Great 27l back) in a Hereford maiden (2m, good) 15 days ago; steps up in trip and holds place claims.

runners_data.name: Madmoiselle Moss
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor form who fades in the finish and faces impossible task off long absence
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in a couple of bumpers and on hurdles debut last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in a couple of bumpers and on hurdles debut last month.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who fades in finish and has been beaten long way in recent similar events over shorter trips
runners_data.comment: Beaten long way in two similar events over 2m at Hereford recently.
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time AW winner at a modest level on Flat; beaten long way in two similar events over 2m at Hereford recently; steps up in trip but easy to dismiss.

races.paceDynamic: Bathara is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a sustainable gallop without pressure through the early stages. The prominent runners Rebel Tribesman and Royal Rocket will track behind, while the majority of the field are hold-up horses including Mr Rafiki, Blue's Secret Gem, The Craftymaster, Madmoiselle Moss and Alex The Great. With so many needing to be produced late and only one natural leader, this creates a tactical race where the pace could collapse in the middle stages. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners and the lone leader, as they'll have positional advantage when the hold-up brigade struggle for racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Bathara gets an easy lead and isn't pressed early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes falsely run which suits his front-running style perfectly, and the hold-up horses behind struggle to close the gap when it matters. Bathara capitalizes on his positional advantage despite his recent disappointing form over hurdles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Success
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman or Royal Rocket successfully track Bathara without making the running
scenarios.body: They get the perfect trip behind the leader and have enough tactical speed to strike when the pace lifts approaching the final flight. The hold-up horses get caught too far back in a slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The stronger stayers among the hold-up brigade can use their class to overcome the positional disadvantage in a messy finish. Mr Rafiki or The Craftymaster could benefit from their higher ratings if they get clear runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Creates Opportunity
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman decides to press Bathara early and they go too fast
scenarios.body: The two leaders compromise each other through honest pace, allowing one of the hold-up horses to come through late. This suits those with proven stamina over the distance.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Rebel Tribesman decides to press Bathara early rather than tracking, as this could set up the race for the hold-up horses
Watch the pace through halfway as with so many hold-up horses this could become falsely run which heavily favors Bathara
Watch Mr Rafiki's jumping on seasonal return as his wind surgery and improved Ffos Las run suggests he's back to form
Watch for traffic problems in the straight as six of eight runners need to be produced late in what could be a bunched finish
Watch Blue's Secret Gem's confidence over the obstacles after her poor hurdles debut at Fakenham 16 days ago

runners_data.name: The Moonlight Man

runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who showed his first form over fences when second of three in a weak contest at Ffos Las (3m, heavy) in March; had excuses when pulled up last time but does need to show improvement.

runners_data.comment: 1-28 under rules, his win coming over fences off this mark at Newton Abbot last July.
runners_data.spotlight: 1-28 under rules, his win coming over fences off this mark at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) last July; has been off since October and needs to hit the ground running.

runners_data.spotlight: Dual chase winner on slow ground (2m/2m3f) but out of sorts last term and has a lot to prove.

runners_data.name: Grand Sabre

runners_data.spotlight: His sole success came here (3m, good) last May off this mark but he's been disappointing since; first-time cheekpieces are applied on his first run for five months and they need to spark him back to form.

runners_data.name: Tom Desjy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 7lb penalty for recent 3m win but prone to fading in finish, fitness advantage from nine-day turnaround
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark on his third start over fences at Southwell nine days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on his third start over fences at Southwell (3m, good) nine days ago; carries a 7lb penalty but this lightly raced type has scope for further improvement and will be hard to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Tom Desjy will take this race along from the front with no other confirmed leaders in this small field. The Moonlight Man, Testflight and John W Creasy are likely to track closely behind the leader, creating a moderate pace that could quicken from three out. The hold-up horses Edgewell, Yes And Yes and Grand Sabre will need the pace to be strong enough to close into, but with Tom Desjy prone to fading and the prominent runners not aggressive early, this sets up perfectly for the closers who can time their challenge late over this stamina-testing trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Tom Desjy sets only a moderate pace and the prominent runners don't apply pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the closers to conserve energy and unleash telling finishes over the final half-mile. Edgewell and Yes And Yes benefit most from this tactical setup with their proven ability to quicken late over extended trips.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Strike
scenarios.trigger: If The Moonlight Man and Testflight press Tom Desjy from early and increase the gallop
scenarios.body: The sustained pace suits horses who can travel strongly in behind the speed without needing to make ground late. John W Creasy could also benefit if finding his old form in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tom Desjy Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the recent winner gets an uncontested lead and his penalty doesn't slow him significantly
scenarios.body: His fitness advantage from a recent run nine days ago proves decisive if allowed to dictate throughout. The lack of pace pressure early allows him to retain enough energy to resist late challengers despite his tendency to fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Returning Winner Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Grand Sabre benefits dramatically from the first-time cheekpieces and extended absence
scenarios.body: The headgear sharpens his focus while the five-month break has refreshed him completely. His course-and-distance win off this exact mark last May proves he has the ability when right.

watchPoints.text: Tom Desjy could get an easy uncontested lead if the prominent runners are sluggish early, making him very dangerous despite his finishing concerns
Edgewell's trainer Nick Scholfield is in decent form at 1/9 in the last 14 days, suggesting stable confidence behind this hold-up specialist
Grand Sabre wears cheekpieces for the first time after five months off - any positive market move would signal the headgear is working at home
The pace could collapse completely with only Tom Desjy wanting to lead, which would severely disadvantage the hold-up horses who need something to aim at
Testflight faces a fitness test after 211 days off but trainer Sue Gardner is 1/6 recently, indicating some stable form behind this returning runner

runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner who has shown significant improvement since fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces in handicaps over fences, winning over C&D (good) 16 days ago; further progress looks nailed on and he should be hard to beat.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen

runners_data.spotlight: Held up; returned to form in March/April, winning at Hereford and Newton Abbot; only just run out of it at Hexham 18 days ago and had no difficulty justifying a confident waiting ride in small field at Huntingdon (again 2m4f on good) last night; highly respected (despite the penalty) if he turns up once more.

runners_data.name: King Of The Story
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner facing tough task from back of field, 26-day break following 5-month absence raises fitness questions despite C&D win
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Fontwell on his return last month following a five-month break.
runners_data.spotlight: Has four wins over fences, including over C&D; encouraging fourth at Fontwell (2m3f, good) on his return last month following a five-month break but he's 2lb higher than his last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Rangatira Jack
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor recent form despite weight drop, 15-day gap reasonable, needs to prove he can recapture April 2023 Exeter form
runners_data.comment: Sole success came at Exeter in April last year; second at Ffos Las 15 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came at Exeter off 7lb higher in April last year; has slipped down the weights but placed for the first time since when second of six finishers at Ffos Las (2m5f, good) 15 days ago; cannot dismiss.

races.paceDynamic: Full Force Gale will set the pace from the front, with only Rangatira Jack potentially joining him in the early stages given both horses' prominent tendencies. Jack Doyen and King Of The Story will settle at the back as confirmed hold-up horses, creating a clear split between front-runners and back-markers. With limited pace pressure on Full Force Gale, he can dictate terms and potentially steal a march on the hold-up horses who will need the race to develop into a strong gallop. This tactical scenario strongly favors the front-running/prominent horses who can avoid the traffic problems that may affect the hold-up pair.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Full Force Gale maintains a steady gallop without serious pace pressure from Rangatira Jack.
scenarios.body: The leader can quicken when it matters most while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from the back of the small field. Full Force Gale's recent C&D win and current form progression make him perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold Up Challenge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with Rangatira Jack pushing Full Force Gale along.
scenarios.body: Both hold-up horses get the strong gallop they need to unleash their finishing kicks, with Jack Doyen's recent form revival making him particularly dangerous. The front-runners pay for their early exertions as the race becomes a test of stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rangatira Jack Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Rangatira Jack can combine his prominent style with a strong finish to bridge the gap between pace-setters and hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: His positioning allows him to track Full Force Gale's moves while staying clear of potential traffic issues affecting the back-markers. Despite his poor recent form, the drop in weights and prominent running style could pay dividends in this small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: King Of The Story Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the veteran can overcome his 26-day break and higher weight to produce his best form from the rear.
scenarios.body: His four fence wins show he has the class when right, and the good going suits his profile perfectly. However, he needs everything to fall right from his hold-up position and faces a tough task conceding weight to in-form rivals.

watchPoints.text: Jack Doyen's recovery from yesterday's run - if showing any signs of a hard race, his chances diminish significantly in this quick turnaround
Full Force Gale's early fractions - if he goes too fast early trying to shake off Rangatira Jack, it opens the door for the hold-up horses
King Of The Story's jumping rhythm early - needs to settle and jump fluently to give himself any chance from his hold-up position
Rangatira Jack's position through the first mile - must stay close enough to Full Force Gale to remain competitive but not exhaust himself
The pace battle between the two prominent runners - whoever wins this early duel likely controls the race outcome

races.paceDynamic: Crest Of Stars and King Of The Road are both confirmed front-runners who will dispute the early lead over this extended trip. With two genuine pace-setters in a small field, they'll likely set a solid gallop throughout rather than crawling early. The testing 2m5f distance at Warwick will amplify any pace pressure, potentially causing the leaders to weaken in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and hold-up horses who can capitalise on a strong early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Clash Early
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Stars and King Of The Road engage in an early battle for the lead
scenarios.body: The two front-runners will compromise each other's chances by going too fast early over this stamina-sapping trip. Prominent runners like Norman Fletcher and Il Va De Soi can track the pace and pounce when the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If either Crest Of Stars or King Of The Road establishes an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The lone leader will dictate a more sustainable pace and prove hard to peg back over this extended distance. Their natural front-running style gives them the tactical advantage when allowed to bowl along freely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If La Vish gets the perfect pace scenario with strong early tempo
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen can utilise La Vish's hold-up style to devastating effect, swooping late when the pace has taken its toll. The testing finish at Warwick suits horses with a strong finishing kick over this stamina-demanding trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders show early restraint and settle into a steady rhythm
scenarios.body: A more sedate early gallop would negate the stamina concerns and favour the most talented horses regardless of tactics. This would bring the better-rated horses like Champagne Twist back into contention despite tactical disadvantages.

watchPoints.text: King Of The Road's breathing after recent wind surgery - any distress signals will end his chances quickly
How hard Crest Of Stars and King Of The Road go in the opening half-mile will determine the entire race outcome
Il Va De Soi's jumping rhythm early - he was fluent when winning here 11 days ago
La Vish's position turning in - needs to be within striking distance to utilise his finishing kick
Norman Fletcher's response when asked for effort - previous struggles at this trip suggest stamina limitations

races.paceDynamic: Buxted Reel and Louie The Legend are the only prominent racers in a field dominated by hold-up horses, meaning they'll set an uncontested early pace over this sharp 2m trip. With six hold-up horses including Westerton, Babychino, Golly Gosh, Allibaba, and Karthala all relying on late kicks, the early leaders won't face pressure until late. Onehundredneighty adds some forward interest but fades in the finish. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can dictate terms and kick clear before the hold-up brigade gets organized.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel and Louie The Legend set sensible fractions without pressure
scenarios.body: They'll have too much in hand when the field full of hold-up horses tries to close late over this minimum trip. The winner comes from these two pace-setters who avoid the traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pair go too fast early or one falters
scenarios.body: The best of the closers can capitalize on a tactical collapse up front. Allibaba's recent win suggests he's the pick of the hold-up horses to time his run perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners hit the wall simultaneously in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A blanket finish ensues as multiple hold-up horses arrive together with similar chances. The winner emerges from a messy finish where positioning matters more than ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Onehundredneighty Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the stable switch to Ben Pauling unlocks hidden improvement and he stays on strongly
scenarios.body: He bridges the gap between pace-setters and hold-up horses by racing prominently without fading. His better finishing kick separates him from the early leaders.

Louie The Legend's early position - if he sits closer than usual he could have too much tactical speed

races.paceDynamic: Kingston Sunflower is the lone early leader but hasn't run for 168 days, creating uncertainty about her fitness to sustain the gallop. Four horses (Bluegrass, Forget The Way, Mojito Des Mottes, Chief Sunday) will be scrapping for prominent positions behind her, creating a bunched field and potential traffic problems turning for home. The hold-up brigade (High Fibre, Brendas Asking, Unjeu Royal, Scintillante) will be relying on gaps appearing in the straight. This pace setup strongly favours the prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the inevitable scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners get into an ideal rhythm behind Kingston Sunflower's moderate gallop
scenarios.body: They'll have first run on the hold-up horses and can kick clear before the back markers get organized. The winner emerges from this quartet with tactical speed to spare.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Kingston Sunflower proves fitter than her 168-day absence suggests and the prominent pack fail to pressure her
scenarios.body: She can string them out with a sustained gallop and hold on, while the hold-up horses are left with too much to do. Her class rating of OR 118 gives her the engine if the fitness is there.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Special
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast trying to reel in Kingston Sunflower and come back to the field
scenarios.body: High Fibre or Unjeu Royal can time their challenge perfectly as the early pace collapses. The winner needs clean splits and a strong jockey ride from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Kingston Sunflower stops quickly due to her layoff and the prominent pack get into a messy early battle
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any hold-up horse with room can win. Scintillante's dual Worcester wins show she can pounce when the pace falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Kingston Sunflower's jumping early - if she's rusty or makes mistakes, the whole pace scenario changes dramatically
